title: -ért and kerül: Asking and Telling Prices

sections.title: Two ways to talk about price
sections.content: mennyibe kerül? ("how much does it cost?") is the standard question in every shop — it uses kerül ("to cost") with the -ba/-be ending you already know: X forintba kerül ("it costs X forints"). -ért is a different, new ending meaning "for/in exchange for" — it never changes for vowel harmony, so it's always -ért, on any word: forintért, ajándékért, pulóverért. Use it when you're paying for or getting something in exchange for a price.

items.english: How much does this sweater cost?

items.spanish: Ezer forintért vásárolom ezt a pulóvert.
items.english: I'm buying this sweater for a thousand forints.

items.spanish: Ötszáz forintért ez nagyon jó ár.
items.english: Five hundred forints is a very good price.

sections.content: mennyi and hány already ask about quantity from A1 — mennyi kiló, hány darab. -ba/-be for cost and -ért for exchange both slot into things you already know how to build; only the endings themselves are new.
